Comments Mike Williams of Southwestern Energy contacted the PADEP Northeast Regional Office Emergency Response Team at 9:29 PM on 8/25/15 to report an estimated (20) gallon diesel fuel release that occurred and impacted the access road on 8/25/15 around 8:45 PM. Hydraulic fracturing operations were in progress on the Oak Ridge Pad when the release occurred. The release occurred due to a sand track shearing the fuel line connecting the fuel tanks on the truck as the truck was travelling up the access road approaching the pad. In order to stop the leaking diesel fuel from the truck and control the release, the remaining diesel fuel in the truck was unloaded into nearby water trucks, drip pans were placed under the truck and absorbent pads were utilized to soak up the diesel fuel on the ground surface.

Sediment was brought onsite for backfill of the remediated area. I observed glass bottles broken and garbage throughout the sediment. Over range reading were observed on the well head (Photo 16 and 17). I observed grease dripping from well head which resulted in accumulating on gravel below. properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/15/2025
Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 8234505
Permit API: 129-25570
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Hempfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/15/2025
Comments: On May 15, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection was conducted to follow up to IR 3944466, where violations were left outstanding due to no Act 9 sign and Emergency Response plan (ERP) onsite. Also, at the time of this inspection, no response of any kind has been received from the operator regarding violations issued in 3093059 or any subsequent cleanup that may have been conducted. At the time of IR 3484420, the soil conductivity onsite appeared to be comparable with that of the surrounding soil. At the time of IR 3944466, no staining or distressed vegetation was observed around the production tanks.The following was observed:No Act 9 sign is present at the well site entrance, and no ERP was found anywhere onsite (see photo 1). The production tanks appear to be sound at the time of inspection, with no evidence of fluids leaking to the ground around them. However, they still lack secondary containment, as is required at unconventional well sites (see photos 2-5). The top hatch of the production tank closest to the well head was not observed on the ground during this inspection. The Department recommended in IR 3944466 that this top hatch be replaced onto the production tank to prevent possible overflowing with rainwater.The well site overall exhibits greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation concerns are observed at this time (see photos 1 and 4). The access road remains stabilized with gravel. The well tag that was affixed to the well head during the time of IR 3944466 appears to have been removed. No staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around the well head (see photo 6). The additional piping and production equipment that does not appear to be in use remains onsite (see photo 7). The Department recommends that equipment onsite that is not in use for production is removed from site. The well postings onsite include contact information for Dorso LP (see photos 8 and 9).Based on observations from this inspection, violations that were continued from IR 3944466 shall remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken onsite since the date of that inspection and no response of any kind to IR 3093059 has been received to date.

SWMA 302(B)3 - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person failed to design, construct, operate or maintain facilities and areas in a manner that do not adversely effect affect or endanger public health, safety and welfare or the environment or cause a public nuisance.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Diversified Oil & Gas Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-12-27
Violation Code: SWMA 302(B)3 - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person failed to design, construct, operate or maintain facilities and areas in a manner that do not adversely effect affect or endanger public health, safety and welfare or the environment or cause a public nuisance.
Violation ID: 872526
Permit API: 129-27282
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: South Huntingdon Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-12-27
Comments: This Inspection is being conducted in response to a complaint that was received by the Department on 12/11/2019 regarding concerns about large rusted holes in the sides of several brine tanks. WQS Eric Norman is assisting. The conditions during this inspection are cloudy in the mid 50's. An Act 9 Sign is at the entrance but is very faded. The Department recommends that the Operator maintain the sign to regulated specifications. The ERP and SDS are on site, the ERP appears to be site specific. The access road appears to be built, with no visible signs of accelerated erosion or sedimentation. The well head is labeled. No leaks or discharges observed. The site appears to be constructed and the well appears equipped for production. Associated production equipment and Production Tanks are on site. The Production Tanks are in an earthen dike. The earthen dike appears to have some holes, possibly associated with nuisance wildlife, the Department recommends that the operator take steps to correct those issues in order to maintain the structural integrity of the earthen dike. The Production Tanks appear to be in poor condition with large holes in both tanks toward the top of both. The Tank closest to the well head appears to have corrosion over most of the tank. No leaks, spills, or distressed vegetation is observed. Inspections 2716702, 2819306, and 2856714 mentioned issues with corrosion and holes in these brine tanks dating back to 04/10/2018. The Department is requesting monthly inspection logs for the Production Tanks from 04/10/2018 until 12/30/2019. The Department is also requesting a time table for correcting or removing these tanks. Based on this inspection, violations are being issued. More violations may be issued based on operator response to the NOV's.

Comments: On August 5, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Mgmt's Armstrong 2 gas well site and direct access road following IR 4160648, where violations were issued for heavily rusted production equipment due to their corrosion posing the risk of a spill and/or release and following IR 4183514, where violations were issued for an inaccurate well tag/posting.A Notice of Violation Operator response has yet to be received for the violations issued during IR 4160648 and 4183514, and site conditions appear to be unchanged from IR 4160648/4183514/4218644.The Department's assessment of the shared portion of this access road as well as the direct portion of this access road can be found in IR 4253879.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the Armstrong 2 well site to be overgrown with vegetation, the Department recommends the Operator maintain the vegetation within the well site to ensure the well site remains accessible. A well tag was observed to be fixed to a heavily rusted gas well that did not appear to have updated Operator information posted on it. Violations issued for an inaccurate well tag are being continued at this time.At the time of this inspection, a heavily rusted production tank was also observed on site and connected for production, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this tank or gas wellhead at this time. The Department recommends the Operator monitor and maintain the structural integrity of the production tank and gas wellhead to ensure that corrosion does not worsen resulting in a release. Although no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed, a strong gas odor and hissing was still observed to be coming from the lower portion of the gas wellhead.Based on today's inspection, violations issues for heavily rusted production equipment posing the risk for a spill/release and for inaccurate operator information on the well tag/posting is to remain outstanding at this time.

Comments: On February 6, 2023, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident response inspection (CTS 369753) at the EQT ARO LLC Elbow Fish and Game Club Pad A. Over the weekend, a line froze that is associated with one of EQT's gas dehydration units causing a pressure relief valve to open resulting in a release of glycol onto the pad surface. The triethylene glycol misted out of the relief valve and impacted a 40 ft. x 25 ft. area around the dehydration unit. At the time of arrival, EQT contractors were wiping glycol off of surrounding equipment. The contractors were beginning to excavate the southeast end of the dehydration unit. EQT is unsure of the amount of glycol that spilled outside of the secondary containment so, EQT plans to remediate the spill under ACT 2.The spilling of glycol outside of containment to the well pad surface is a violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Solid Waste Management Act Section 301, and Chapter 78a.56(a).

Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator of a release of an estimated 5 gallons of hydraulic fluid to the pad surface on Pad B. He showed me the location of the release which was along the edge of the well site secondary containment in the travel lane near the company man trailer. The company man said that the release had occurred from a radiator on a cement truck that was offloading into the upright cement tanks at the time. This sump was installed after fluid with elevated conductivity was discovered by the Department in that area of the pad. The electrical conductivity of the fluid in the sump was approximately 1350 uS/cm. The area around the sump on the pad surface was dry during this inspection. Violations remain outstanding in association with this release.

Comments: This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack that appears to have been recently produced. A sticker is posted on the pump jack displaying the operator's information, the well's API number is written on the jack. There was no activity onsite during this inspection. An approximate 2' x 5' area of vegetation and soil are stained with a coating of crude oil on the well site from the apparent repeated venting of this well into the atmosphere. The same practice is prevalent at a majority of the well sites on the Warrant 2980 lease and will be addressed in a separate inspection report. A tank battery that is located approximately 250' southeast of well consists of four steel and six plastic storage tanks inside of an earthen diking. There are several areas of stained gravel near the tanks (and at a compressor that is also located inside of the diking) which is indicative of production fluid releases onto the gravel inside of the containment.The exterior (southern) wall of the diking is void of vegetation and the specific conductance (SPC) is elevated (3800 uS/cm per field meter). It appears that the production fluid that has been released into the gravel inside of the tank battery diking has migrated through the southern wall of the containment and into a roadside ditch that flows south towards a cross culvert approximately 200 feet south of the well. Stressed vegetation, elevated SPC readings and abundant deer tracks are present in the ditch between the tank battery and the cross culvert and continue in a channel down to the next lease road (near 053-29533) approximately 300 feet beyond the culvert outlet.Multiple sections of the Warrant 2980 lease roads beyond this well to the vicinity of well #'s 053-29907, 053-29935 and 053-29916 have not been sufficiently maintained. BMPs (ditches and cross culverts) that are installed along these roads are not functioning properly, as a result, accelerated erosion is occurring over various stretches of the road surface. Additional E and S concerns on this lease are documented in the 5/11/23 inspection report for 053-29536 (Warrant 2980 #37).It is requested that documentation of production water disposal from this lease be provided to the Department. Comments: On 07/18/2023, an incident inspection was conducted at the Ironman Well Site in response to an incident report received by the Department and submitted by EQT on 07/17/2023 (CTS: 373620). I was accompanied by Matt Dracup, PGM (PADEP), Doug Oberdorf, and Jason Nicholson (EQT). Additional EQT and SPSI representatives on site. Stressed vegetation observed on north-northwest facing slope (fill side) of the Ironman pad on 07/14/2023 by an EQT contractor doing a routine site inspection. EQT representative investigated stressed vegetation on 07/17/2023 and identified it as a brine release and notified the Department. It was further investigated by EQT on 07/17/2023 w/ interim remediation activities starting on 07/18/2023. According to EQT, an approx. 5 ft x 2 ft pool of fluid was observed within area of stressed vegetation and fluid was observed sprinkling out. The overall area of stressed vegetation was approximately 25 ft x 25 ft. The release was estimated over a barrel and Act 2 remediation is anticipated. The source of the leak was identified as a small pinhole in cushion elbow at the northern most corner of the pad from the buried common dump line transferring brine flowback from the GPUs to the ASTs; approx. 70 ft northeast, away from the stressed vegetation area. Operator discovery and pre-remediation conductivity levels and incident writeup requested.Inspection observations: Area of stressed vegetation and pooled production fluid observed on fill slope below northwestern edge of pad and below compressor building on the pad. Among pooled fluid, an oily sheen was also observed. The impacted area appeared to be approx. 25 ft. x 25 ft. The area was covered with a plastic tarp upon arriving on site (Photos 1-7). SPSI crew preparing and beginning excavation to locate source of leak and begin remediation measures. Potholes to be dug on pad around approximate area of leak source to gain extent of fluid. Elevated conductivity observed within impacted area yielded readings of 14.62 mS, 9.96 mS. Readings beyond edge of impacted area, on the more northern edge of the area, displayed a reading of 1.87 mS. Additional readings within vegetation beyond edge of affected area were taken and yielded levels of 1.03 and within the area beyond the fence approximately 5 ft. at the bottom of the slope, 1.98 mS was observed within vegetation. Readings taken within the Unnamed Tributary to Daniels Run, below impacted area approximately 125 ft. north of the impacted area. Readings obtained within water and sediment of the stream w/ levels at 0.43-0.86 mS. Readings obtained within retentive berm along southeastern edge of site below pad; readings taken in water and within sediment yielded 0.33 mS and 0.60 mS (8-16). Readings taken at southern corner of the vegetated swales outlet structure, both in and around; readings of 0.46 mS within water and 0.59 mS within mud around the structure observed (17). SPSI began excavating a pothole, approx. 3 ft in depth; pooled fluid observed within. Conductivity reading within excavated hole was 6.30 mS. Vegetated berm adjacent to hole, above impacted area, displayed a reading of 0.34 mS (18-20). Additional readings within vegetation beyond western edge of impacted area displayed 2.21-6.44 mS (21-23). Reading in fluid contained within secondary containment around ASTs w/ level of 7.20 mS. Due to observed release of production fluid within vegetation on site and potential for fluid to impact WOC downslope of impacted area, violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued. Additional violations of 78a.66(b)(2) for failure to report within 2 hours, 78a.66(b)1(i), 78a.66(b)1(ii), and 91.33(a) for threatening WOC pollution, 5 gallons not completely contained and failure to report to DEP and downstream users are being issued. Additional follow up inspections to be conducted to monitor WOC downslope of impacted area.

Comments: The site of this oil spill is in a forested area on an access road south off Center Hill Road, 430 yards on south branch of access. Will Warfel contacted WQS Taylor and reported to National Response Center that there was a release of about 20 gallons of crude oil from a tank the wind tipped over in one of the recent storms. The path of the crude oil was ~320 yards on the access from origin of the spill to low spot where it left the road and seeped into the stream. Blobs of oily material were found ~60 yards downstream. Two absorbent booms were placed in the stream along with absorbent pads. One absorbent boom was placed across the access road and one was positioned along the road to catch any remaining oil from seeping to stream. Visual clean-up of oil and oil contaminated soil completed where the tank tipped and leaked oil. The tank was removed and contaminated soil piled and covered until soil is tested and can be received at a licensed facility.Violations for the release of oil to ground and into a stream issued with this inspection. Clean-up, restoration and stabilization of spill site with vegetation and receipt of tipping receipts and waste manifest by the Department required to lift violations.

Comments: On November 19, 2025, the Department conducted a Partial Routine inspection on the access road of the Breese well site in Buffalo Township, Washington County. During this inspection, the Department observed torn Compost Filter Sock (CFS) installed in the roadside ditch of the access road entrance. This torn CFS was overtopped by sediment which accumulated in the roadside channel (photos 2 and 3). This deep accelerated erosion rill appears to be the source of the scouring and sedimentation shown in Photos in 2-5, due to the potential for channelized stormwater flow.Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued against the overtopped CFS and the accelerated erosion and sedimentation in the access road.

Violation ID: 960863

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 7/05/2022
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a Follow-up Inspection (FUI) of the Seneca Resources - DCNR 007 Pad K Well Site located in Delmar Twp, Tioga Co. on 7/5/22 @1045 hours. The weather was 70 degrees, light rain, winds S @5mph. Seneca Company Man, Travis Deleon was present onsite.During the previous inspection (IR#3376280) dated 6/10/22, a damp area and puddle was observed below the hose connection to the Highland production tank. The puddle had a field measured conductivity of 11.02 mS/cm. Sample 4427-261 was collected from the standing fluid and submitted to the DEP laboratory in Harrisburg for analysis. The sample results show the presence of a pollutional substance. Barium was reported at 44.78 mg/L, strontium was reported at 166.9 mg/L, and chlorides were present at 3410.8 mg/L. As of today's inspection, a small piece of secondary containment was observed installed under the hose connection on the rear side of the Highland storage tank. The area under the secondary containment was observed damp with a small amount of standing fluid. A Groline soil conductivity meter was used to measure the field conductivity of the damp soils from 1.97mS/cm - 2.37 mS/cm. A comparison of the previous photo taken of the area during the inspection on 6/10/22, to the current state of the area, indicates no pad material was removed from the impacted area. I spoke with a Seneca representative onsite and he stated production would be dispatching someone to the site to remediate the area today. A vac truck arrived onsite and removed the remaining production fluids from the Highland tank and drained the secondary containment. I again spoke with an onsite well tender regarding the removal of impacted pad material. He spoke with Jim Westbrook and stated Gas Field Specialists had been dispatched to the site and would arrive this afternoon. I completed my inspection and departed the site at 1300 hours. Gas Field Specialist personnel located me while conducting an inspection at the nearby Pad D. I informed them of the area with elevated conductivity on Pad K, where they were headed, and we discussed removal of the impacted pad material. They requested I return to the site after they had removed the impacted material to screen the area with a soil conductivity meter. None of the GFS personnel or onsite Seneca representatives possessed a conductivity meter. The impacted pad material was removed with shovels and 5 gallon buckets and placed on temporary secondary containment. I screened the excavated area for soil conductivity and found readings of less than 800 uS/cm. The area was backfilled with clean material and the secondary containment was repositioned under the hose connection. GFS personnel said they would provide the cleanup information and pictures to Seneca for followup with the DEP.Violations of the following regulations remain outstanding against API#117-22143 165HU awaiting the information requested in the NOV issued in IR#3387022 :CLS 402(b)SWMA 30125 Pa Code 78a57 control, storage and disposal of production fluids25 Pa Code 78a66(b)I again departed the site at 1530 hours.

The sample results show the presence of a pollutional substance. Barium was reported at 44.78 mg/L, strontium was reported at 166.9 mg/L, and chlorides were present at 3410.8 mg/L. As of today's inspection, a small piece of secondary containment was observed installed under the hose connection on the rear side of the Highland storage tank. The area under the secondary containment was observed damp with a small amount of standing fluid. A Groline soil conductivity meter was used to measure the field conductivity of the damp soils from 1.97mS/cm - 2.37 mS/cm. A comparison of the previous photo taken of the area during the inspection on 6/10/22, to the current state of the area, indicates no pad material was removed from the impacted area. I spoke with a Seneca representative onsite and he stated production would be dispatching someone to the site to remediate the area today. A vac truck arrived onsite and removed the remaining production fluids from the Highland tank and drained the secondary containment. I again spoke with an onsite well tender regarding the removal of impacted pad material. He spoke with Jim Westbrook and stated Gas Field Specialists had been dispatched to the site and would arrive this afternoon. I completed my inspection and departed the site at 1300 hours. Gas Field Specialist personnel located me while conducting an inspection at the nearby Pad D. I informed them of the area with elevated conductivity on Pad K, where they were headed, and we discussed removal of the impacted pad material. They requested I return to the site after they had removed the impacted material to screen the area with a soil conductivity meter. None of the GFS personnel or onsite Seneca representatives possessed a conductivity meter. The impacted pad material was removed with shovels and 5 gallon buckets and placed on temporary secondary containment. I screened the excavated area for soil conductivity and found readings of less than 800 uS/cm. The area was backfilled with clean material and the secondary containment was repositioned under the hose connection. GFS personnel said they would provide the cleanup information and pictures to Seneca for followup with the DEP.Violations of the following regulations remain outstanding against API#117-22143 165HU awaiting the information requested in the NOV issued in IR#3387022 :CLS 402(b)SWMA 30125 Pa Code 78a57 control, storage and disposal of production fluids25 Pa Code 78a66(b)I again departed the site at 1530 hours.

Inspection Date 2016-12-20
Comments Inspection of Range’s Hess 1H in Morris Twp. Clearfield County conducted December 20, 2016 at 1:00 pm. The rig has rigged down and pulled off the pad following last week’s plugging operations. At the time of inspection; the well was capped with night cap bolted on (5 1/2”) production casing spool. There was a ½” needle valve on the cap, shut-in. I opened the valve, no pressure, and tied in with a ½” pex fitting with hose connected to an Altair 5x gas meter. The meter showed 4% LEL at first then dissipated in a few seconds to no gas detected. I put a balloon on a ½” pipe nipple and threaded into the needle valve to verify no measurable flow. The balloon did not inflate. There was a 2” vent pipe for the backside of production casing (9 5/8” x 5 ½”) production casing plumbed to surface. The vent was open to a small poly tank with and had a ½” ball valve in line. I opened the ½” ball valve and heard gas even as the 2” line was open to the poly tank. I shut in the ½” ball valve in line and the 2” ball valve to the polytank, threaded a 0-160PSI pressure gauge on the ½” ball valve and opened it to the pressure gauge. The pressure on the vent exceeded the pressure gauge in one second. I allowed the well vent another minute and tried again; same result. This is a violation of 25 PA Code § 78.91. General provisions

EQT indicates assessment will focus on dump line trench and northern pad slope, but does not discuss WOC.Due to the deficiencies noted within the 15 Day Report, a violation of 78a66(c)2i is being issued for the failure to provide a complete initial written report within 15 days. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PA GEN ENERGY CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/03/2024
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8203048
Permit API: 081-21985
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/03/2024
Comments: Arrived onsite for a routine inspection. It was about 57F and sunny.Compost filter sock infiltration berms were installed on the northern side of the pad. The berms were in various stages of vegetative growth but appeared to be functioning properly.Plugs were being drilled out and flowback was expected to begin in the next couple weeks. Overall, the site was clean and organized. The secondary containment appeared to be in good condition. However, some fluid with elevated conductivity of 5.59 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm) was found on the pad surface on the southwestern part of the pad (Photos 3-5). The fluid was observed between a set of frac tanks and a vacuum. Due to the elevated conductivity, sample 0719-287 was collected.Other puddles on the pad surface were screened and had conductivity readings below 0.7 mS/cm. The PCSM and surrounding areas were also screened and no impacts were observed. Before leaving the site the PGE representatives present were notified and immediately began removing the fluid from the pad surface. Due to the unknown volume, origin, and time of the release, it is strongly recommended that remediation be completed under Act 2 requirements. Additional screening should also be performed on and around the pad to determine the extent of potential additional impacts. The result of this inspection is Violations Noted for CSL 402(b). Additional violations may be cited based on the pending results of sample 0719-287.

Comments: This inspection focuses on multiple discharges from various tanks that are located in the proximity of this well. An approximate 210 bbl portable steel stock tank is actively discharging crude oil from a corroded part of the tank. The fluid is currently discharging at a minimal rate and likely only occurs during hot, sunny conditions which liquifies the residual paraffin at the bottom of the tank. At this time, there is approximately 10 gallons of free crude near the tank and a 5' x 10' area of oil soaked ground downslope of the discharge point. A second tank with the same issues is located to the south of this well. The nipple located on the bottom of a steel stock tank located west of this well has failed and resulted in an approximate 1/2 barrel of crude oil to discharge onto the ground, within an earthen containment. GPS coordinates of these incident sites are provided in the photographs included in this report. The well itself is equipped with a pump jack, a site ID sign is posted on the location.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Pin Oak Energy Partners Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-02-19
Violation Code: 78A57(A)___ - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator discharged brine and other fluids on or into the ground or into the waters of this Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 878216
Permit API: 047-24535
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Saint Marys City
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-02-19
Comments: This inspection was performed following a report of a possible spill/breached containment at the Beechwood Pad A site. (CTS #348135). The site was inspected for evidence of lack of secondary containment around equipment and/or spills. The production fluid tank site was inspected. This site contains three 400 barrel tanks. It appears from the staining on the tanks that they have overflowed at some point. The containment is filled with snow that has not fully melted. The area behind (on the north side) of the tank site was checked and there was some liquid beneath the ice in the ditch. This liquid measured between 2 mS/cm to over 6 mS/cm conductivity on the Spectrum Soil EC probe. It appears as though a leak occurred at this site at some point, which the operator allowed to escape containment through some means and enter the ditch line. The overflow detection system appears to have been turned off at this tank site. Also on site was a gas/liquid separator which was fed by several types of fluid. The fluids were contained in their separate containments. The separator was set in containment that had blocks set up for holding tanks that have been removed. The containment itself was dry and it was noted that there were several holes in the liner, which would allow any spilled fluid to leak out of containment. The area around the wellheads is clean and no evidence of spills was noted. The site ID sign is on site with well and pad information.

Comments: On 12/18/2025, an incident inspection was conducted at the John Briggs Well pad in Aleppo Township, Greene County for a reported release (CTS: 394097). I was accompanied by DEP Water Quality Specialist Sara Trio.The spill was reported to the Department by the operator on 12/11/2025 through the DEP Emergency Hotline. It was reported that the piping inside the 50U Gas Processing Unit (GPU) washed out and produced fluids spilled off containment and onto the well pad. The amount reported was greater than 5 gallons and the spill was contained to the well pad. Specialized Professional Services, Inc (SPSI) was on site the same day to begin clean up.The following was observed during the inspection:- The spill area was observed adjacent to the 50U GPU. The impacted gravel was excavated. Absorbent material was observed behind the GPU (Photos 1-3).- Conductivity readings were taken throughout the spill area. Elevated conductivity was observed in two small holes sumps that collected fluids (Photos 4-6). Elevated conductivity was also observed behind the GPU near the absorbent material (Photo 7).- Additional conductivity readings were taken throughout and outside of the spill area. They were all observed to be below clean up standards (Photos 8-12).It appears the spill still needs additional remediation in certain areas. The Department requests information on the amount spilled and how the amount was verified.Violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued for the spill.

Comments: On 11/17/23 an incident inspection of the Coastal Greene Well Site was conducted in response to the report of a spill received by the Department on 11/17/23. Background:On 11/17/23 Greylock self-reported a brine release on the Coastal Greene Well pad. On 11/17/23 I spoke to Keith Eighmey of Greylock to acquire additional details about the spill. During the inspection it was determined that an estimated 10-15 barrels of impaired water had been released to the pad surface from a failure of the 8MH GPU unit. Investigation showed that the release was contained to the pad area and no water ways were impacted. Mr. Eighmey said that Greylock would have equipment, a containment, and a roll off box on site by 1-2pm on 11/17/23. Findings:-An act 9 sign was present at the entrance to the well site (Photo #1).-The spill is suspected to have originated from the 8MH GPU units (Photo #2,6).-Standing water and a wet spot was observed around the GPU units (Photos #2,3,5,6,8,9).-Elevated conductivity was observed in standing water around the GPU units (Photo #4,7). -Crews were present on-site working to repair the GPU units. (Photos #2-6). -No elevated conductivity was observed outside of the spill area.No impacts to WoC were observed. Violations of 78a57(a), SWMA 301, 78a54, and 78a64(a)b are being issued for the release of brine to the ground and failure to have the GPU units in secondary containment for a well drilled in 2018.

Comments: On April 17, 2026, an on-site meeting was held at the operator's request at the former location of the MAWC well pad in Springfield Township, Fayette County. The purpose of this meeting was to assess current vegetative growth and review areas lacking 70% vegetative growth coverage. This also a follow-up inspection to IR 4175984.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) was executed between the Department and the operator on December 16, 2021. The First Modification to the COA was entered on May 1, 2025. Paragraph 3i of the 12/16/2021 COA states: "M4 shall immediately commence work to completely restore the Well sites upon execution of the First Amendment and complete restoration of the Well Sites by October 30, 2025, in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas act, 58 Pa.C.S. 3216, the site restoration regulations set forth in 25 Pa. Code 78a.65, and all applicable provisions of the Clean Streams Law and the regulations promulgated thereunder. M4 shall submit form 8000 PM-OOGN0075, "Well Site Restoration Report," within sixty (60) days of restoring the Well Sites."Site restoration is to be conducted "as closely to original conditions as practicable, including restoration of original contours and capability of supporting land uses existing prior to drilling of the Well(s) by October 30, 2025, unless M4 obtains a signed and notarized written consent of the landowner to leave the Well Site in an altered state".The following was observed during the inspection:The former well site appears to have overall established additional vegetative growth since the time of IR 4175984; exhibiting approximately 50% vegetative growth during this inspection. The temporary stabilization applied on site appears to be adequate at the time of inspection. Additional reportedly third-party vehicle tracks were observed at the former well pad location (photos 3, 5, and 10). Daugherty reported that the landowner installed signs at the site entrance that prohibit vehicular use on site (photo 14). The Department recommends that the operator continue to document any third-party disturbances occurring on site, take reasonable efforts to stop them while promoting continued vegetative growth, and prevent accelerated erosion from occurring on site.The super silt fence remains installed at the northern boundary of the former well site (photo 13). Daugherty reported that it is to remain installed as during site restoration as an Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) control measure. It appears that the portion of it located within the site boundaries have been repaired and maintained in accordance with current regulations. The Department recommended during this inspection that the operator continue to maintain the super silt fence in accordance with manufacturer specifications, if it is to remain in-use during site restoration.No loose sediment was observed in the channel that empties into the Sediment Trap that reportedly pre-exists well site construction (photo 11).Minor areas that appear to be susceptible to receiving high winds and concentrated stormwater flow were identified on site during this inspection. The Department recommended during this inspection that the operator consider additional E and S control measures to prevent potential displacement of mulch and seed, such as erosion control blanketing.While leaving site, the Department observed that Daugherty had started work on site with an overseeder.Based on observations from this inspection, the violation issued in IR 4095466 shall remain outstanding.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation ID: 968350
Permit API: 015-23708
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Asylum Twp
Inspection Type: Drilling/Alteration
Inspection Date: 9/14/2022
Comments: On 9/14/2022, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Chesapeake Hopson well site. It was 75 degrees and partly cloudy when I arrived on location. I met Joe Button at the entrance to the site. He said that the area that was identified in previous inspections as having elevated conductance had been uncovered. We went to that area and I used an Oakton PCTS 50 to sample a water puddle in that area with the current result of 0.924 mS conductance. I used a Hanna Groline tester to sample gravel and mud in that area. A 10'x20' area gave readings from 1.5 mS to 3.0 mS. I probed areas outside this location with results less than 1.0 mS. I checked other water/mud puddles on the site with the results ranging from 1.6 mS down to less than 1.0 mS. Joe said that Chesapeake would have a crew on site tomorrow to scrape the affected area.Joe and I went down the fill slope to the rock area that I had identified in previous inspections with elevated conductance. Today the reading was 2.05 mS conductance. I discussed with Joe actions to prevent this water from getting off site. The department took samples from this location in a previous inspection, the results not yet available. I field tested the soil in the bottom of the south end of infiltration area 1 with the result being 0.31 mS conductance.A crew was on site reinstalling the gas pipeline to transport gas off site. Another crew was preparing the 10 wells for production. Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed on site by two retentive grading/infiltration areas. Infiltration area 2 does not meet the 70% uniform perennial vegetative requirement.The DEP recommends the following:1. Proceed with Act 2 for the area with elevated conductance.2. Intercept and capture the fluid with elevated conductance identified on the east fill slope as close to the source as possible to prevent the fluid from leaving the site and causing contamination to the waters of the Commonwealth.3. Continue to monitor the stability of infiltration area 2 and provide additional resources as necessary to achieve at least 70% uniform perennial vegetation.I left the site at 15:00 hrs.

Comments: Inspection 2 of 2On 06/03/2025, an incident inspection was conducted at the NV55HS Well Site following receipt of a spill report. The spill was reported to the Department on 06/02/2025 at 10:58am (CTS 389543). I was accompanied by Bruce Carpenter of CNX. Additional CNX representatives and SPSI were on site. The spill was reported to have occurred on 06/02/2025 at 7:30am. It was reported that produced water sprayed under the pad from one of the valves on the GPU. The release was contained and an unknown quantity was reported. No waterways were affected. The following was observed:Behind the GPU, a seep is present. Flow from this seep has allowed water to pool on the pad. This area was actively being vacuumed to remove any production fluid within the area. Absorbent materials were in use on site (Photos 1-3).Conductivity readings in the pooled area on the pad ranged from 375 uS/cm - 9.94 mS/cm (Photos 4-9).The water leads to a collection box on the pad, that outlets downslope of the pad. The shut off valve had been closed after the spill. No elevated conductivity was noted at the outlet off pad (Photos 10, 11).The operator updated the Department on 06/05/2025 that spill remediation has been completed. The Department requests an updated estimation of amount of fluid spilled. The Department also requests that a waste manifest be submitted as soon as possible. Due to the current estimated amount of fluid released being 4-5 gallons but threatening pollution to the Waters of the Commonwealth, and reporting the spill later than 2 hours after discovery, violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b) are being issued.

Comments: On December 7, 2018, the Department performed an inspection of the CNX RHL22 well pad site. The site is located in Richhill Twp., Greene County. The inspection was a follow up inspection related to a reported reuse water release to the well pad on 12/1/18, and violations issued on 12/3/18. The operator initially reported a 30 barrel reuse water release to the well pad @ 01:15 a.m. on 12/1/18. The operator did contact the Department at 11:00 a.m. on 12/1/18 to report that the release was greater and was approximately 210 barrels of reuse water. The operator has reported that during the transfer of reuse water from the constructed MASS on the tank pad, along the access road, to the working tanks a communication error occurred and the working tanks were over filled causing a release of approximately 210 barrels of reuse water to the well pad. The reuse water overwhelmed the well pad secondary containment discharging to the well pad and storm water collection channels for the site. The reuse water then entered the PCSM structure discharging off site. The collection channel to the PCSM was also overwhelmed and the water was discharged onto the RHL28 gathering pipeline ROW adjacent to the well pad site. The operator was excavating impacted material off site on the pipeline ROW at time of inspection. The operator was also excavating the PCSM and PCSM collection channel at time of inspection. The operator was using field conductivity readings to direct the excavation activities. The operator had attempted to plug the PCSM discharge structure, with an inflatable rubber plug, but was unable to do so. The Department observed elevated conductivity readings in the standing water and soils on the southwest corner of the well pad, as well as the storm water controls for this area. Elevated conductivity readings were also observed off the well pad site on the pipeline ROW and down gradient from both sites during the 12/3/18 inspection. The operator has completed hydraulic fracturing operations on the site and has begun removing the equipment necessary for hydraulic fracturing from the well pad. The operator has reported to the Department that secondary containment will be setup on the well pad to store excavated, impacted soils for disposal and remediation efforts will continue all weekend and into next week on the well pad as well as in the PCSM structures impacted by the reuse water spill.

Violation ID: 998676
Permit API: 083-47406
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/15/2023
Comments: This was an inspection performed following a report that the operator had a leaking brine tank on the Enis Lease. I inspected all three tank batteries on this lease.This well is producing and is equipped with a gas powered pumpjack. No spills or leaks are noted at the well. There is a tank battery near the well with two 210 barrel stock tanks contained. There is a buried brine tank across the access road in a wooded area. It appears that there has been an ongoing small leak in the tank, which has allowed brine to leak out into the soil. Impacted soil is apparent ~35 linear feet from the tank, at the base of a small hill. A check with a soil EC meter showed conductivity ranging from 1.5 to 5 mS in the soil. The liquid, along with deer activity, has stripped away vegetation from a 10x15 foot area. The water does not appear to have traveled much further than this and does not appear to be a threat to enter the waters of the Commonwealth.After this visit, I called the operator and he came to the site a little later to look at it with me. He agreed that the tank appeared to be leaking. I suggested that the tank would need to be vacuumed out, removed from the ground and the impacted soils remediated. He said that he would be contacting a contractor immediately to begin this process. Continued followup will be done as necessary.
